notes: Chief/owner creation requires title, project_id, and an explicit kind. For binary goals, include primary_checklist_block_id: null explicitly selects binary completion; a saved checklist block ID selects that checklist. For quantitative goals, include a non-null primary_chart with an explicit chart kind and completion_rule. Create the input measure before the goal. Goal kind alone does not select the main display. Send the object to panels goal create on stdin.

Defaults for other fields: why empty, active true, deadline null. Binary completion defaults false. Quantitative completion comes from its rule and retained evidence. Omitted page defaults to an empty headroom.page version 1 with the goal title and empty summary. Replace measure_example in both the chart and completion_rule with an existing measure. Example dates and targets are illustrative.
Use panels goal schema edit for changes and panels goal schema primary-chart for chart author input.

Replace placeholder IDs with existing records. Page block and checklist-item IDs can be omitted and are generated. SegmentedView IDs are required. Saved component IDs must be nonempty and unique. Sections need exactly one of blocks or views.

deadline is an ISO calendar date or null. kind is binary or quantitative. A supplied page is a complete page-kit document, not a partial patch. Completion and active state remain independent. A quantitative chart does not determine completion. New quantitative goals require completion_rule, separate from progress targets. Existing legacy goals retain their state until explicitly configured.

completion_rule compares actual and target expressions with direction atleast or atmost. first_date is the earliest permitted achievement date. Both expressions use the existing measure formula language. Actual must reference retained measurements; constants alone cannot complete a goal. Panels records the first supported success date automatically. Later fluctuations preserve that milestone; corrections and rule edits reevaluate it.

Checklist items accept an optional deadline as an exact YYYY-MM-DD calendar date. Omission or null means undated. Set a date, replace it, or clear it with null through the ordinary page edit. Example dates are illustrative; choose dates from the user's requirements. Item dates do not change overall deadline, completion, or active state.

Goal pages are dashboards for the user. Keep them focused on useful signals and concise text. Use checklists for steps and charts for measurements. Add text when it gives useful context rather than repeats visible state. Include intake records or work artifacts only when they help the user. Preserve useful authored context and artifact previews.
Goals belong to a holder. Set holder_kind to chief with holder_id null, or manager with the saved Manager ID. Talk about goals through the holder conversation.

A chart has type chart and a separate kind such as line. Use direction atleast or atmost (not target_direction). The example target 100 is an explicit illustrative test assumption; choose the real target from the goal's requirements.

Chart id can be omitted and is generated. Primary chart placement defaults to primary; charts in page blocks default to supporting. An explicit primary_chart placement must be primary. Keep accepted IDs when you edit existing components.

measure_id must name an existing measure. Formula expectations require a measure-bound, nonstacked line or number without aggregates or manual controls. Category bindings, manual controls and other chart kinds retain their existing semantic checks.

notes: Read panels goal show GOAL_ID --json first. Send changed fields to panels goal edit GOAL_ID on stdin. Omitted goal fields stay unchanged. Authority checks run before the existing document validator.

A kind change requires the destination main-display choice in the same request: binary needs primary_checklist_block_id, including explicit null for binary completion; quantitative needs a non-null primary_chart and completion_rule. A configured numeric rule cannot be cleared while the goal remains quantitative. Manual completed writes must agree with automatic completion. A selected checklist must exist in the resulting page, including nested layouts. If a page edit removes the selected checklist, explicitly select a replacement or binary completion. A quantitative goal cannot clear its main chart without an explicit valid display switch. Ordinary edits preserve existing and legacy display configurations.

Before an item-date edit, copy the accepted page from goal show and keep every block, item ID, state, and unrelated field. Change only the intended item's deadline. The workshop examples are complete fictional pages; never replace a real page with an example page.
